items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: with the First Sergeant who conducted, Sergeant Baraka was a doll. And I remember on my birthday... he knew my birthday, I was invited to his house for dinner.

ctx.x: That’s like figuring out codes and all that.

Yeah, yeah. I’d be probably a CIA guy or something. Isn’t that funny? I mean I know it was a choice you know. So I was put into the band and I was stationed in Westover Field in Springfield, Mass in a Military Air Transport Command — MATS. And I played in the band and they ran the — you know from Westover they used to go to Germany, I can’t think of the name of it, it’s still there, the Air Force base. Wiesbaden, and then there was the name of a Air Force base. And they’d go back and forth and stuff. And they…

he knew my birthday, I was invited to his house for dinner. And there I am and I didn’t drink at the time, maybe I had a beer or something, and he starts playing these V-disks, and he had Lester Young’s [scats], what is that?
